Marathon Petroleum rose 1.47% today as oil markets tightened on escalating U.S. economic pressure against Iran. The Treasury sanctioned a UAE bank branch used for Iran's shadow banking on the same day the Navy blockade sharply reduced Iranian oil exports—both moves compress global oil supply. For a refiner like MPC, less Iranian crude in circulation can support prices for the oil it needs to process, and the company's refineries are running at 97.4% capacity, meaning they're operating at near maximum throughput to capitalize on current margins.

The stock has climbed 3.79% over two weeks as geopolitical risk to Middle Eastern oil supply has intensified. The conflict has now stretched six months with no resolution in sight, keeping traders focused on supply disruption rather than a near-term end to the tension.
